book: Section 29: associativity of the crossed-product multiplication (29.1) on monomials is equivalent to the factor set condition (29.2); the change of basis v_sigma = c_sigma u_sigma and the principal factor set (29.3); Exercise 29.1 (normalization); the commutation x u_sigma = u_sigma sigma^(-1)(x) used in the corrected display (29.11) of the proof of (29.9).
limitations: Only monomials a u_sigma, modelled as pairs (a, sigma), are treated, over a commutative ring with a group acting by ring automorphisms; the extension of associativity to sums by bilinearity, the crossed-product algebra itself, its simplicity and the tensor product C = A (x) B of (29.9) are not constructed. The tensor-product form (x (x) y)(u_sigma (x) v_tau) = (u_sigma (x) v_tau)(sigma^(-1) x (x) tau^(-1) y) is the factorwise application of mul_unit_eq_unit_mul_inv and is checked only in Sage.

book: Section 29, proof of (29.22): from Schur's identity (29.21) for the matrices P^(sigma), taking determinants gives f(sigma, tau)^m c_(sigma tau) = c_sigma sigma(c_tau), so f^m = delta c; and [A]^m = 1 gives exp [A] | m.
limitations: The matrices P^(sigma) and the identity (29.21) are hypotheses: the module V, its dimension m = (V : L) = index [A] and the action of u_sigma are not constructed, nor is the Brauer group; exponent_dvd_index is the general monoid fact applied to [A].

book: Section 30, proof of (30.3)(iii): in (L/K, sigma, a), (c u)^n = c sigma(c) ... sigma^(n-1)(c) u^n, and the product is N_(L/K)(c) when Gal(L/K) is generated by sigma of order n; with u^n = a this is (c u)^n = (N_(L/K) c) a.
limitations: The identity is proved in an arbitrary monoid for an element u with u x = sigma(x) u on a sigma-stable set; the norm formula needs a finite Galois extension generated by sigma. The cyclic algebra itself, the isomorphism criterion of (30.3)(iii) and its converse direction are not formalized.

book: Section 6, proofs of (6.7) and (6.18): with n = x^2 - x and x_1 = x + n - 2 x n, x_1^2 - x_1 = 4 n^3 - 3 n^2 = n^2 (4 n - 3); iterating, x_k^2 - x_k lies in N^(2^k) and x_(k+1) - x_k lies in N^(2^k) when x^2 - x lies in N.
limitations: The identity is proved in an arbitrary ring. The membership statements are proved for an ideal of a commutative ring (the proof works in the commutative subring generated by x); the N-adic topology, the convergence of the sequence, the limit idempotent and the lifting of orthogonal decompositions (6.19) are not formalized.

book: Section 10, proof of (10.8): if Lambda = Lambda' (+) J with Lambda' = {x in Lambda : x e = 0} (e a central idempotent of A) and J a left ideal of Lambda, and r (1 - e) lies in Lambda for some nonzero r in K, then J = Lambda e, e and 1 - e lie in Lambda, and Lambda' = Lambda (1 - e) is a ring with unity 1 - e; this is the step that makes Lambda' an R-order in A' in the induction.
limitations: The splitting Lambda = Lambda' (+) J (from the projectivity of the Lambda-lattice Lambda e by (10.7)) is a hypothesis; orders, lattices, hereditary rings, the left hereditary property of Lambda' and the induction over the simple components are not formalized.

book: Section 14, proof of (14.6) and Exercise 14.5: the matrix pi_D^* (entries 1 at (i, i+1), pi at (n, 1)) has determinant (-1)^(n-1) pi, so nr pi_D = (-1)^(n-1) pi; the n-cycle i -> i + 1 (mod n) has sign (-1)^(n-1), the sign in the corrected congruence det a = (-1)^(n-1) pi N_(W/K) alpha_1 (mod pi^2 o_W).
limitations: Over an arbitrary commutative ring, for the explicit matrix only. That the n-cycle carries the only term of det a not divisible by pi^2 (when alpha_0 lies in pi o_W) is checked symbolically in Sage for n = 2, ..., 5, not in Lean; the skewfield D, the reduced norm and the Hasse invariant are not formalized.

book: Section 33, end of the proof of (33.12): for q >= 2, a divisor s of n with 0 < s < n and 0 < t <= n - 1, lambda = (q^s - 1) t (q - 1) is positive and smaller than q^n - 1, so q^n - 1 does not divide lambda (the corrected range 0 < t <= n - 1 and bound with n - 1); the printed bound with n - 2 is 0 for n = 2 while lambda = (q - 1)^2 > 0.
limitations: Natural-number arithmetic only, with s <= n/2 used in the integer form 2s <= n instead of the real bound (q^(n/2) - 1)(q - 1)(n - 1). The Frobenius automorphism, the intermediate fields of W/K and the congruence q^s t (q - 1) = t (q - 1) mod q^n - 1 are not formalized.

book: Section 37: proof of (37.36)(ii), gamma = n phi with phi an isomorphism gives ker gamma = (Cl Lambda)_n and cok gamma = Cl Lambda / n Cl Lambda; proof of (37.40)(i), exactness of (37.39) at Outcent Gamma and n-torsion of (Cl Lambda)_n give f^n in im alpha; (37.40)(ii), Out_R M_n(R) = (Cl R)_n forces f^n inner.
limitations: Group theory only, for arbitrary commutative groups A, B, C and groups G, H. Picent, Cl, Outcent, the maps alpha, beta, gamma, theta, phi, zeta, the identity gamma = n phi (Exercise 37.3) and the exactness of (37.39) (Snake Lemma) are hypotheses, not constructed.

book: Section 39, end of the proof of (39.14): the matrix Pi with 1 on the subdiagonal and pi_D in the top right corner, the generator of rad Lambda_0 = Lambda_0 Pi for the order with all invariants 1, satisfies Pi^n = diag(pi_D, ..., pi_D); this is the matrix identity behind (rad Lambda_0)^n = pi_D Lambda_0 and J^(re) = pi Lambda (39.18)(iii) for this order.
limitations: The identity is proved over an arbitrary (not necessarily commutative) ring for the explicit matrix. The lattice statements (that Lambda_0 is an order, rad Lambda_0 = Lambda_0 Pi, Pi normalizes Lambda_0) are not formalized; they are checked on explicit cases in checks/sage/s39_hereditary_local.py.
